steps.title: Keep a permitted complete installed Windows player
steps.instruction: Use an already permitted, fully working v1.3.1 Windows x86-64 reblue.exe installation with all of its creating runtime, original-derived game tree, profiles, mods and companions. Select the installed executable at its established root, not the freshly extracted setup copy or a repair/updater/build helper. The ordinary release uses DirectX12; a separately built Vulkan variant is not inherited. Project BSD3 terms do not license original game data, optional DLC or all private/generated/component material.

steps.title: Complete all three supported originals upstream
steps.instruction: Finish the normal upstream wizard with all three disc images from your own supported Global US/EU Blue Dragon copy before registration. Keep one supported set, its originals, recorded fingerprints and full resulting installation; Asia/JP or arbitrary cross-region/revision mixing is not established. Upstream marker/container/title checks and fingerprints are not Core exact three-disc authentication. The wizard copies itself, restarts, installs game files and writes its registration outside Core; wait for that preparation and any repair to finish. Core does not parse/assemble/generate/admit the triple.

steps.title: Settle replacement and recovery before selecting
steps.instruction: Finish any pending upstream update or recovery and a normal upstream start/quit before registration. Do not delete or ignore .update staging, ready markers, replaced-file or recovery history as a workaround: startup can apply a staged update and relaunch before the update-check setting is read. Turn the normal upstream startup update/content check off for this route. A new download, update, repair or backend/warm reboot must be completed externally before the next reviewed Play; Core does not adopt its successor.

steps.title: Select the installed player and its exact paths
steps.instruction: Select root/reblue.exe with the actual installed-root working directory and one literal --game_data_root=<absolute prepared game-data directory> argument (ordinarily root/game containing default.xex for this upstream installer), --profile=<actual existing profile name>, and --no-bd_update_check. Keep spaces inside each single token; these are arguments, not a shell command. The game-data directory must belong directly beneath that same creating installation root: its parent becomes the profile/cache root and must match the installed executable directory. Preserve an established supported custom direct-child tree rather than rename it or select an unrelated external directory. Explicit game_data_root selects that installation independently of shared install lookup; default.xex presence alone is not full original or private-output validation. The bound normal Windows entry runs its application/message loop in process. Keep any other supported working flags exactly; generic SDK user_data_root/cache_root flags do not override the title’s profile/cache routing.

steps.title: Preserve every actual original and player root
steps.instruction: Keep the whole external install, complete originals/private output, game-data tree, mods, installed DLC/content, logs, root/cache, profiles/<actual name>/reblue.toml, profile saves/achievements/content and unknown files, plus all legacy roots and existing shared HKCU installation registration. Preserve actual bd_saves_path and bd_cache_path overrides separately. The title uses the selected installation’s profiles/name as its user root; save/cache overrides and prior layouts are distinct. Do not reset profile/configuration, repoint shared registration or regenerate a private copy merely to register. Core neither backs up these roots nor claims safe save/profile migration or rollback.

steps.title: Review launch details and manage your copy
steps.instruction: Consent to the exact native executable, working directory and literal arguments, then choose Play separately. A current library-owned installation or active registration/launch cannot be bypassed by this alternative. Existing managed/source contracts remain unchanged; selecting an external copy grants no managed generation, immutable private-output certification or source admission. The program can make normal profile/DLC/cache writes, and its UI can reenable checks; this is not a sandbox or an all-network-off promise. Normal ordered shutdown has a default1.5second forced-exit watchdog, so process exit is not clean-save certification. Close all real instances before upstream changes, retain the old creating runtime/data together and relink changed executables. Registration-only removal preserves all external files.

warnings: This is the conditional Windows existing-player route. No game package/original/private save/compiler/installer/upstream helper/game was acquired or executed for this source/fixture batch; actual game/save/DLC/profile compatibility, installed Desktop, physical/human, other-platform and protected acceptance remain separate.

No Core-managed installation, three-disc preparation, generation, update, backup, rollback, migration, registry rewrite or external deletion is offered. The existing strict definition/source history and all earlier failures/qualification facts remain intact; no Supported or other-platform promotion.

steps.title: Prepare the PS4 remake with upstream first
steps.instruction: Use a complete copy and components you are independently permitted to use. The reviewed 0.70 Windows route is the Bluepoint2018 PS4 remake: CUSA08809 EU1.01 or CUSA08034 US1.00, with your own decrypted game folder containing eboot.bin, sce_module and sce_sys. PS2/PS3 releases are different inputs. Sound additionally needs your own console-dumped decrypted libSceNgs2.sprx and libSceUlt.sprx; those Sony modules are not supplied by this guide or covered by the runtime license. Follow upstream setup outside Portcove, select the correct game/modules and save settings before attachment.

steps.title: Keep the complete Windows package together
steps.instruction: The inspected0.70 SotC-PC.zip contains SotC-PC/SotC.exe, bin/bb-probe.exe, companion DLLs, _internal, scripts and launcher resources. Keep the entire extracted SotC-PC directory together in a writable location. SotC.exe is the frozen native frontend; selecting an internal probe, Python executable, DLL or original eboot.bin bypasses its saved setup. This registration does not download, extract or run setup.

steps.title: Select saved-settings play explicitly
steps.instruction: Select the prepared package’s SotC.exe, set its complete SotC-PC directory as working directory, and use the single argument --play. Review the exact selected intent, then request Play separately. With a valid saved game folder, this route waits for its --run child, which in turn waits for bin/bb-probe.exe. If setup is missing it opens the GUI instead: finish setup and close that attempt before retrying. No native run or child-cleanup observation is claimed by source inspection.

steps.title: Preserve all actual data locations
steps.instruction: The current package keeps launcher_settings.json in its user directory; the ordinary save/cache/log root is also user beside SotC.exe unless the saved user_dir or existing SOTC_USER_DIR selects another location. Keep the complete effective tree, sotc.ini, any legacy %APPDATA%/sotc-launcher/settings.json, original game/update/DLC folders and your console modules. The source can discover neighbouring -UPDATE/-patch folders and established source/data overrides. This guide sets no new override, moves no saves and promises no cross-copy or cross-version compatibility.

steps.title: Leave maintenance and shutdown with their owners
steps.instruction: Complete upstream updates, setup changes and repair outside an attached game session; the GUI updater can start an applier/successor. Close the actual game and all helpers before replacing files, retain independent recovery copies, then review/relink changed executable bytes. Let ordinary play end through the game before closing the tracked player. Forced termination is not proof of save flush or child quiescence. Portcove does not adopt updater successors or own runtime replacement.

steps.instruction: Preserve the project GPL notice and all component/NVIDIA notices; runtime licensing grants no rights to the original game or console firmware. steps.title: Download the upstream setup package
steps.instruction: Extract the complete official setup ZIP for your system into a separate writable folder you control. Its launcher builds the game using your own matching disc. On Linux, follow that version’s prerequisites, including CMake, Ninja, Python 3 and a C/C++ compiler where required; bundled Windows tools do not supply Linux tools. Downloading and extracting do not start setup or the game. Portcove has not confirmed setup or gameplay for this package.

steps.title: Supply the matching original files
steps.instruction: Follow the upstream guide for the version you downloaded. Use your own original in its supported image representation, keeping a CUE and every referenced track together when required, and supply your own BIOS whenever that guide requires it. Preserve the exact edition, disc layout and BIOS requirements in that guide; an included setup BIOS does not establish game compatibility.

steps.title: Finish upstream setup, then add the player
steps.instruction: Open the project’s launcher to build the game from your own files. Follow the instructions for that version and keep the completed game with its required runtime and compiler files. In Portcove, select the completed game executable or supported launcher and its working folder. If setup created the game elsewhere, select that location. Save the launch details, then choose Play when you are ready. You manage updates, original files, saves and settings; Portcove does not back up these external files. Keep a working copy and its data before changing versions.

steps.title: Choose your own USA disc
steps.instruction: On first Play, choose your own MediEvil II USA SCUS-94564 CUE with its BIN tracks, or a supported CHD, in the native launcher. The disc remains required. listings.name: Valkyrie Profile / Alexbeav PSXRecomp
listings.summary: PlayStation port prepared with your own matching disc and any required BIOS. Complete setup with the project’s launcher; you manage this copy, its updates and your saved data.

steps.title: Finish the upstream setup package first
steps.instruction: Use the complete official v0.1.3 Windows x64 setup package in a separate writable folder. Its root executable is a setup host, not the completed player. Deliberately finish upstream Generate & Build with your own matching originals and its required tools before adding the player. The existing Linux setup download remains separate: use the complete Linux package and this version’s prerequisites, including CMake, Ninja, Python 3 and a C/C++ compiler where required; bundled Windows tools do not supply Linux tools. The Windows completed-player steps here do not qualify a Linux player. The standalone flow is supported; RetComM is an optional upstream manager. Portcove does not start a compiler, helper or installer while discovering a launch target.

steps.title: Keep both USA discs and your BIOS
steps.instruction: Use your own complete canonical USA disc pair, SLUS-01156 and SLUS-01179, keeping each CUE with every referenced track, and your own legal SCPH-1001 BIOS. OpenBIOS is not qualified for this title. The published first-track identity is not a complete two-disc verification. Upstream reports one corrected Windows Disc 2 operator test; that does not establish every transition, save/reload or future rebuilt version.

steps.title: Add the completed native player
steps.instruction: Select build-release/Valkyrie_Profile_Recompiled.exe, or the actual completed product in your upstream-configured build directory. Use its containing directory as the normal working folder, preserving a different established working directory if your actual working launch requires it. A normally prepared product needs no extra arguments; retain any actual supported --game plus absolute configuration path, disc, BIOS or memory-card arguments used by your working copy as separate literal arguments. Do not select the root setup host, which can forward to another executable and exit. Save launch details, then choose Play separately.

steps.title: Preserve the complete creating project and profiles
steps.instruction: Keep the whole setup project, both original discs, BIOS, generated sources, build-release or custom build directory, dependencies, game.toml, game_options.toml, settings.toml, sidecar .cfg files, cards, saves, states, mods, caches, logs and unknown files. Runtime paths anchor to the actual executable, with some source paths searched above it; inspect the actual settings and preserve custom paths and both root/build histories. You or upstream manage rebuilds and updates. Portcove registration provides no managed backup, update, rollback or migration; removing registration leaves every external file untouched.

warnings: Project-owned GPL terms do not grant rights to original game data, generated retail code, BIOS or separately licensed dependencies. Keep private prepared outputs private unless their applicable terms permit sharing.

listings.name: Diablo II: Resurrected — Reign of the Warlock (d2r-mobile)
listings.summary: An experimental Diablo II: Resurrected-specific ARM64 compatibility project using Metal/Vulkan. Broad mobile playability and performance are project claims; the early Mac version has keyboard/gamepad limits described in its guide. setup.sh prepares patched modules and shaders locally, and mac_app.sh builds a Mac app; DM_MAC_M3 selects the older API. iOS shell ZIPs and Android/HarmonyOS shell files still need your own runtime and game data, and updates require rebuilding. Documented platforms are Apple Silicon macOS 26+ or older API 15–25, iOS 26 or older API 18–25, and Android ARM64 API 31+/Vulkan 1.1; Intel is unsupported. HarmonyOS has separate community support, while tvOS is only a character-selection preview. Use your own Switch game and required expansion 1.0.34.0 (PC 3.3.94012), matching ExeFS/RomFS and prod.keys for extraction. Other build IDs are unconfirmed. Supply your own ClayFighter63⅓ USA and ClayFighter:Sculptor's Cut USA ROMs. After normalization to big-endian z64, their SHA256 values must be 357f26c6cd72559c5c05e8c2df46369624630dbcb1c02b3b6f3338f6ac79af07 and 9ccebc317b7ee892be3bdc0d1c8ae46687995908ed51ebd58d6855e5e25abd7f, respectively. steps.title: Complete permitted upstream asset installation
steps.instruction: Use a complete v2.1.1 Windows x86-64 copy and components you are independently permitted to use. The GPL licence for authored port code does not grant rights to packaged branding, depicted original characters or the separately supplied title announcement. On Windows 10/11 x64 with an SSSE3/SSE4.1 CPU and current Vulkan drivers, run Install Assets.vbs outside Portcove and finish asset installation. The included Python runtime checks both inputs and creates local imported files. Keep all supplied DLLs, configuration, notices and assets together.

These are the same native arguments used by the upstream Play wrapper. Do not select VBS/CMD/Python installers or unfinished data. The native player owns the game window and normal game loop. Saving launch details and requesting Play require separate consent.

steps.title: Preserve imported files and settings
steps.instruction: Before first prepared startup, moves or updates, close the game and keep a separate complete recovery copy of local/, probe-output/, config and all original ROMs. Imported files include probe-output/base.z64, local/sc_roster/asset-image-roster.z64, local/sc_bios/bios.bin and local/import-manifest.json. Upstream installation replaces its generated outputs; reinstallation requires both originals. Keep current player settings separate from an older runtime backup.

steps.title: Keep portable custom profiles inside the game
steps.instruction: Display, native game options, P1/P2 controls and training settings live in local/settings/ by default; graphics caches live under local/cache/. The executable locates its installation from its own directory/config and changes CWD to it. Optional --data-dir or --user-data selects a profile only inside that installation; outside paths and escaping symlinks are rejected. --controls imports a profile but subsequent edits save inside the installation. Preserve every selected in-root profile, temporary/recovery copies and any custom source controls before maintenance.

steps.title: Keep maintenance upstream-owned
steps.instruction: The player and upstream own asset extraction, runtime replacement, settings and recovery. Portcove registers the explicitly selected prepared native copy; it does not acquire the originals, run extraction, update or delete external data. Finish upstream maintenance outside a tracked session, retain a complete previous runtime and current player data, then revalidate the selected executable. Do not infer compatibility between fused data, other editions or different builds.

steps.title: Respect component and edition boundaries
steps.instruction: Retain the GPL authored-code licence and individual SDK/RT64/SDL/Python/Microsoft notices. NOTICE explicitly excludes the branding and supplied replacement announcement from the code licence; obtaining another full package needs an applicable independent grant for those components. The optional title announcement falls back to the original ROM audio when absent, but this guide does not prescribe modifying a package or bypassing its grants. Both-ROM fusion identity and upstream claims do not establish full gameplay or save compatibility.

warnings: Fresh acquisition of packaged branding/title media remains conditional on its own applicable permission; original-game rights are separate.
Only an already prepared independently permitted complete copy is offered; extraction, updates and recovery remain upstream-owned.

steps.instruction: If you are not using the Windows Setup wizard, the supplied conversion scripts expect raw disc data at install/Driver2CD1.bin and install/Driver2CD2.bin, with config.ini pointing to the first image. steps.instruction: Play opens crispy-doom-setup.exe. Configure controls and use F2 Warp for single-player launch; choose your actual Final Doom campaign there. The chooser can expose other detected IWADs; Portcove does not restrict or check your campaign selection. The main-menu launch command forwards its existing arguments. The PWAD/mod browser is not an original-IWAD browser. This entry uses one saves folder and can share save slots if you switch campaigns. Do not switch this entry’s campaign in place: its retained runtime versions share data. Use a separate Portcove library or independently owned upstream copy for the other campaign or another source variant. No automatic switching or cross-campaign save compatibility is established. An upstream setup exit does not establish that the game loaded or ran successfully.

steps.title: Keep the declared private data scope
steps.instruction: Portcove retains originals deliberately copied under originals, this entry’s default configuration, saves under saves, known default save locations, numbered screenshots and declared recording files. Put custom recordings under demos or use a demo-prefixed .lmp filename. Upstream may read and write its music-pack profile on Play. steps.title: Select the actual player and CPU build
steps.instruction: Prepare a complete official Windows FreeSpace Open player copy compatible with your CPU and data, keeping its DLLs. The inspected x64 SSE2 package’s normal player is fs2_open_26_2_0_RC3_x64_SSE2.exe; select the actual compatible fs2_open player executable from your prepared copy, not FRED, a dedicated server, installer or mod manager. Keep the retail root as working directory and the established literal -mod and other supported arguments. Launcher-only setup is not reproduced by selecting an engine executable.

steps.title: Retain all creating data and preference roots
steps.instruction: Keep the complete game root, data, mods, launcher settings and all actual player/pilot/campaign files. Current FreeSpace Open normally uses the current account’s AppData/HardLightProductions/FreeSpaceOpen preferences on Windows. FSO_PREFERENCES_PATH can redirect it; -portable_mode uses local paths, and legacy settings or failed profile lookup can change the effective location. Retain the effective preferences root, cmdline_fso.cfg, logs, captures, custom and unknown files. Preserve any launcher-provided environment; attaching a standalone player does not reconstruct it.

steps.title: Check the prepared copy before registration
steps.instruction: Finish setup with the project’s tools, then start and quit the copy you intend to add. Keep its game executable, working folder and supported launch arguments. Review those details in Portcove and agree to launch them, then choose Play separately. Adding a copy does not confirm its original game files, gameplay or save compatibility.

steps.title: Keep updates and removal under the existing owner
steps.instruction: Close every running copy of the game before changing files. Keep the working game version and every data and profile folder recoverable. Update it with the project’s tools, then review and select the changed executable in Portcove before choosing Play. You manage setup, updates, file changes, data migration and recovery. Portcove monitors the process you selected; it does not prevent other copies from running or restrict the game’s file access. Removing the registration leaves external files in place. This route does not offer Portcove downloads, setup, updates, backups, rollback, data migration or external-file deletion.

warnings: Use only a copy and content you are already permitted to use. Engine licensing does not grant rights to original game assets, music, mods or bundled components.

listings.name: Geometry Wars: Retro Evolved 2 (Geometry Wars 2 Recompiled)
listings.summary: Prepared Windows Geometry Wars 2 copy using your own matching XBLA package. Upstream owns setup, runtime replacement and portable player data; Portcove can record the ordinary native player separately from Play.

steps.title: Prepare an authorized upstream copy
steps.instruction: Use an independently obtained, authorized Windows copy and the selected upstream guide. The GPL license of the project does not cover the original game or automatically cover every bundled component: the pinned TRG launcher revision has no explicit license file. Automated acquisition needs a separate rights decision. Preserve the complete package, runtime libraries, configuration and notices in a writable folder; do not register an updater or installer. Before the first upstream startup, make separate backups of any existing Documents/geometry_wars_retro_evolved_2 profile and portable user_data/ profile; a successful upstream migration removes the legacy folder.

steps.title: Install your own matching Xbox 360 original
steps.instruction: Deliberately finish upstream setup outside Portcove using your own Geometry Wars: Retro Evolved 2 XBLA LIVE package, title 584108FF and content type 000D0000. The extracted default.xex must be 704,512 bytes with SHA-256 6D5D9980A1D17DC74B9CCF540CEC16C2E144E7CEE3A74938E78C237B8ACEEB88. Individual container hashes can vary. The launcher installs the game into adjacent game/. A container or another Xbox title is not a substitute for this executable gate.

steps.title: Add the prepared native player
steps.instruction: Choose geometry_wars_retro_evolved_2.exe with its containing package folder as the working folder and no arguments for ordinary Play. Its built-in launcher starts the game in the same native process. Finish setup and any update or setting that requires Restart before adding or starting a tracked session; Restart and the separate updater may replace the process. Saving launch details and Play are separate actions. Use the actual selected copy, not a guessed path.

steps.title: Preserve original and player data
steps.instruction: Upstream/player remains the only runtime-replacement owner. Preserve game/, user_data/, logs/, the executable TOML and any chosen custom roots before changing versions. Portable user_data/ contains the 584108FF profile/local scores, achievements, cache and launcher settings. Before the first upstream startup, back up the legacy Documents/geometry_wars_retro_evolved_2 profile and any portable user_data/ profile separately. When upstream migrates legacy data, it moves the legacy folder by rename, or uses a staged verified copy and then removes the legacy folder after activation; successful migration does not leave the old profile in place. A failed migration falls back to the legacy root for that run and retries on the next startup. If only legacy cleanup fails after activation, portable user_data/ stays active and the legacy folder may remain. An unwritable portable root can also fall back to the system root. --user_data_root=<folder> selects that root without migration; --cache_root can select a separate cache. Preserve every active root and the separate backups. Portcove does not own these external files or promise backup, rollback, save compatibility or deletion.

warnings: This guidance follows upstream source and release descriptions. Portcove has not inspected the package or tested launch, gameplay, saving or updates. Experimental Linux AppImages are a separate route.

steps.title: Prepare the correct PS4 game and update upstream

Follow its first setup outside Portcove and keep independent originals before creating its merged game folder. Its preparation uses hard links where possible: a merged tree is not an independent backup of original file contents. No original, DLC, extractor, Python helper or game is obtained or executed here.

steps.title: Keep the complete selected Windows implementation
steps.instruction: The inspected CTR-NitroFueled-PC-portable-windows.zip contains CTR-NitroFueled-PC-portable/CTR-NitroFueled-PC.exe, bin/sacredfire.exe, bundled python, scripts, DLLs and resources. The ordinary frontend is an AMD64 native Windows launcher, not the older Python launcher or a standalone game exe. Keep the whole matching package. This is the existing GetLostIn Windows adaptation of SacredFire with its own maintained Windows layer/launcher and credited upstream fixes; a common game title does not merge it with the separate online fork or qualify the parent’s Linux route.

steps.title: Select and retain the normal launcher session
steps.instruction: After upstream setup, select CTR-NitroFueled-PC.exe, use its complete extracted portable package directory as working directory and leave arguments empty. Review and consent to the selected launch details, then choose Play separately. This opens the upstream launcher; request its Play only when ready. The native frontend waits for its Python runner, which waits for sacredfire.exe. The runner loops over its own Apply and restart exit code, retaining the ordinary waiting chain. Quit the actual game before closing the frontend; its Stop game and quit action forcibly terminates the job and is not a save-flush guarantee. Portcove has not tested this launch-and-quit sequence.

steps.title: Preserve the actual data and hard-link sources
steps.instruction: Keep the whole package user tree with savedata, cache and trophies, the separate backups and DLC directories, launcher.ini, bbport.ini, patches.json, logs and the full prepared game view. Keep the original base/update/DLC sources independently too. The runner normally uses user for saves/cache, while an established BB_USER_DIR or other data/mod/config override can select additional external roots; preserve every effective location. Do not edit a hard-linked merged source as though it were an isolated disposable copy. This guide performs no save import, migration, backup or deletion.

steps.title: Leave replacement and recovery with upstream
steps.instruction: Complete upstream updates, first preparation, repairs and source-root changes outside an attached session. Close all actual players/helpers before replacing files, keep independent recovery copies, then review/relink changed executable bytes. Normal waiting/restart source paths do not establish observed forced-stop cleanup or save consistency. Portcove does not own the mutable upstream runtime, merged originals, backups or external player data. Removing registration preserves all external files.

steps.title: Retain permission and platform limits
steps.instruction: Preserve GPL 2-or-later and all packaged third-party/NVIDIA/font notices; these grants do not grant original-game or DLC rights. Upstream playable race/audio/controller/save reports remain upstream claims; shader stalls and experimental upscaling/frame-generation/ultrawide limits remain. This guide does not establish Portcove gameplay, multiplayer, save/reload, installed-app or Supported acceptance. No managed install/update/rollback/backup/removal is offered.

steps.instruction: Use a complete permitted OpenGothic Windows copy and your own Gothic II: Night of the Raven data. Select native Gothic2Notr.exe with its matching resources/libraries. Gothic I, Gothic II Classic and existing 32-bit Union/AST/Ikarus plugins do not inherit compatibility from this route. Finish setup upstream rather than selecting an installer or a helper.

steps.title: Preserve the actual working directory as well as game data
steps.instruction: Retain the creating working directory and established literal -g argument pointing to the actual absolute Gothic II data root, if used. Automatic discovery is not a reason to change a working data selection. The selected Windows code uses working-directory Gothic.ini and log.txt, separately from original System/Gothic.ini, and writes save_slot_0.sav/save_slot_N.sav relative to the working directory. Preserve the complete creating working directory, actual original-data root, every save/config/mod and unknown file; do not assume the original vendor save directory contains all OpenGothic state.

steps.title: Check the working copy before registration
steps.instruction: Finish setup with the project’s tools, then start and quit the copy you intend to add. Keep its game executable, working folder and supported launch arguments. Review those details in Portcove and agree to launch them, then choose Play separately. Adding a copy does not confirm its game files or save compatibility.

steps.title: Keep updates and removal under the existing owner
steps.instruction: Close every running copy of the game before changing files. Keep the working game version and every data and profile folder recoverable. Update it with the project’s tools, then review and select the changed executable in Portcove before choosing Play. You manage setup, updates, file changes, data migration and recovery. Portcove monitors the process you selected; it does not prevent other copies from running or restrict the game’s file access. Removing the registration leaves external files in place. This route does not offer Portcove downloads, setup, updates, backups, rollback, data migration or external-file deletion.

warnings: Use only a copy and content you are already permitted to use. Engine licensing does not grant rights to original game assets, music, mods or bundled components.
Before updating the game, keep a copy of its working files and every location containing saved data. Choosing a different executable does not give it a separate profile.

listings.name: Gran Turismo 4 (PlayStation 2) (GT4Recomp)
listings.summary: Windows x64 GT4Recomp official launcher for an upstream-prepared Gran Turismo 4 USA v2.00 installation. Register GT4Recomp.exe; its normal owned session supplies renderer configuration, launches and watches the game, then returns to the launcher. Preserve installation data, AppData save libraries and legacy roots before its automatic migrations/cleanup. Branded artwork grants remain separate from the code licence; use an independently permitted complete copy.

steps.title: Use a permitted installation and exact owned disc
steps.instruction: Use an independently permitted complete GT4Recomp v1.2.5 Windows installation and your own Gran Turismo 4 USA v2.00 SCUS-97328 plain ISO. Upstream pins the 5314478080-byte ISO with SHA-256 67b6c0075837f3ae1132d608acf2858bf13b2dd62d6eae83dff76df02e4e824f and verifies prepared CORE/ELF identities separately. Keep the original separately; identity checks do not grant game-data rights. NOTICE defers the bundled cover and brand-art licence to its owner; the MIT code licence does not grant those components.

steps.title: Finish official upstream setup
steps.instruction: Complete the official installer and launcher disc setup outside Portcove. The launcher copies the ISO, verifies preparation, installs the renderer and checks CPU/Vulkan requirements. Use supported Windows x64, SSE4.1 CPU, Vulkan 1.2 and WebView2; retain the complete matching installation and DLLs. This route uses the official launcher, not the internal gt4vulkan.exe with a guessed environment or another version's renderer.

steps.title: Back up all current and legacy roots before first startup
steps.instruction: Close the game and launcher; keep a separate complete prior installation and current <install>/data, %APPDATA%/GT4Recomp, %LOCALAPPDATA%/GT4Recomp and Documents/Gran Turismo 4, including any moved-name sibling or recorded previous installation data. Include settings, controls, Saves, Replays, card backups, runtime/card.ps2, original/prepared disc data, custom textures and configured read/fallback roots. Keep the backups outside old installation cleanup targets. Startup can move user and large data, flatten textures and remove the old per-user program/game folder, fixed shortcuts and registry entries. The running installation and its data-folder layout are excluded from that legacy cleanup; do not rely on an old executable folder as your recovery copy.

steps.title: Register the official outer launcher
steps.instruction: Select GT4Recomp.exe from its complete creating installation, use its installation directory as working directory and leave arguments empty. Start only when a separate GT4Recomp instance is not already running; a second launcher can merely bring the first forward and return. Portcove tracks the selected launcher session, not game-only play time. Save launch details and consent to Play separately; then use the upstream launcher's Play operation.

steps.title: Let the upstream launcher own the game session
steps.instruction: The launcher stays alive, hides to the tray during Play and watches its child game; when the game exits it harvests the card and returns Home. The launcher supplies required renderer environment, config, per-session files and card locks. Quit/save through the game, wait for the upstream launcher to finish card handling, then close the launcher to end the selected session. Closing it while playing asks first and can end the game through its kill-on-close job. Do not register an internal payload, bypass the owner or assume closing Portcove provides a save checkpoint.

steps.title: Preserve effective saves and recovery paths
steps.instruction: Large data normally stays in <install>/data; a nonwritable install may read that folder while writing to %LOCALAPPDATA%/GT4Recomp. Per-user settings, controls, save/replay libraries and card backups normally use %APPDATA%/GT4Recomp, with upstream fallback/read layers retained during migration. Before Play the launcher builds the runtime card from its library, then harvests after exit; do not edit card/library files concurrently. It prunes older session folders to 20 and may rewrite corrupt update metadata to .json.bad. Preserve all current/fallback/legacy roots before maintenance; do not assume cross-version save compatibility.

steps.title: Keep update and restart transitions upstream-owned
steps.instruction: Upstream owns setup, renderer downloads/updates, runtime replacement, data movement and recovery. A launcher update starts its installer and exits; WebView recovery can restart the launcher in safe mode. Complete these transitions outside the registered normal session and revalidate the resulting launcher. Portcove does not reproduce renderer environment, follow replacement processes, acquire originals or delete/restore external data.

steps.title: Retain component terms and known limits
steps.instruction: Keep MIT code notices, the separately GPL-licensed GSdx/PCSX2 renderer notices and source, and all other component notices. NOTICE leaves branded cover and artwork permission unresolved; new downloads of the complete package require the applicable permission or an independently permitted complete copy. Check upstream’s limits for licence demos, menu backgrounds, wheels, long sessions and hardware. Portcove has not confirmed game execution or save compatibility with this launcher route.

warnings: Use an independently permitted complete installation; bundled brand/cover artwork permission is a separate acquisition condition.
Track the official launcher session and let it own preparation, renderer environment, card handling and ordinary game launch. Optional installer/WebView restarts are not followed.

listings.download_block_reason: Fresh acquisition of the selected branded GT4Recomp Windows package is held while the applicable permission or authorized-source basis for its bundled cover-front artwork and derived brand assets remains unresolved. NOTICE leaves the cover-art licence for owner confirmation; the MIT code grant does not resolve it. Resume on an attributable applicable basis or a reviewed supported de-branded package/preparation; independently permitted complete installations remain separate.

listings.name: NBA JAM: On Fire Edition (OpenJam)
listings.summary: Attach an independently permitted, prepared OpenJam Windows player for your purchased NBA JAM: On Fire Edition XBLA copy. The published player already contains recompiled code; upstream setup prepares your game data, with separate per-mod save roots.

steps.title: Prepare your purchased On Fire Edition data upstream
steps.instruction: Use a complete copy and components you are independently permitted to use, with your own purchased Xbox Live Arcade NBA JAM: On Fire Edition container. The 1.1 release manifest identifies LIVE content type 000D0000 and title ID 584111EC; other NBA JAM editions, trial entitlements and arcade ROMs are outside this route. Finish the Mod Manager’s upstream unpack/data/UI preparation outside Portcove, retaining the original container and complete outputs. Setup does not generate the game’s native code in this selected release: the inspected published player already contains it. No original, unpacker, mod, compiler or game is obtained or run here.

steps.title: Keep the complete actual Windows player unit
steps.instruction: The inspected OpenJam-v1.1-win64.zip contains AMD64 nbajam_ofe.exe, NBA JAM Mod Manager.exe, rexruntimerd.dll, rexgpu-xenosrd.dll, TracyClientrd.dll, metadata and controller notices. Keep the whole matching package with the prepared default.xex/data/UI tree. The manager is setup/mod administration; the normal prepared player is nbajam_ofe.exe. Do not select an original XEX, profiler, DLL, mod package or another platform’s shell script. Portcove has not tested dependency loading or gameplay.

steps.title: Select the completed normal game
steps.instruction: Select nbajam_ofe.exe in the complete prepared game folder, use that folder as working directory and leave arguments empty. Review and consent to the selected launch details, then choose Play separately. The source defaults the game root to its executable’s folder and enters its native game application in that process. Complete initial unpacking, UI repair and missing-data work outside an attached attempt. This does not execute the manager or authorize an unowned game/trial entitlement.

steps.title: Preserve separate base-game and per-mod saves
steps.instruction: Keep the entire prepared installation, including default.xex, data, metadata, ui, ui.original, mods, mods.list, saves.path and the complete saves tree. Each mod’s own saves.path can select a root relative to that mod or an external location; preserve every effective destination. Do not combine per-mod saves: the source explains that identical roster slots can mean different players, so sharing them can corrupt progression/unlocks. Also keep any established config, user-data and title-update roots, original containers and independent recovery copies. Portcove performs no save import, migration, backup or deletion.

steps.title: Complete mod switching and maintenance upstream
steps.instruction: The upstream mod system can create successor game processes when switching mods. Complete switching, install/remove, source updates, data/UI repair and runtime replacement outside an attached session; close every actual player/helper/successor before changing files, then review/relink changed bytes. Mods can share unchanged game files through hard links, so preserve independent originals rather than treating a mod tree as an isolated backup. Quit normally; forced termination is not a save-flush or quiescence guarantee.

steps.title: Retain permission and acceptance boundaries
steps.instruction: Keep all upstream, SDK/runtime, controller and component notices. Framework/port terms do not grant EA original-game rights, fonts/art extracted from your own game or separately acquired PS3 mod rights. Upstream gameplay/mod reports remain upstream claims; invalid-texture-fetch warnings and the unmapped clips path remain documented rough edges. No Portcove gameplay, mod/save/reload, installed-app or Supported acceptance is asserted. Removing registration preserves all external files; managed install/update/rollback/backup/removal are not offered.

warnings: Keep the full prepared game and each mod’s actual saves.path destination; mod switching may start a successor and hard-linked mod data is not an independent original backup.

steps.title: Keep upstream ownership and all active data roots
steps.instruction: Upstream/player owns runtime replacement. Preserve game/, logs/, the executable TOML and the complete user_data/ tree: settings.toml, 58410A18 local scores, achievements, cache and 0000000000000000/58410A18 DLC. Before the first upstream startup, back up the legacy Documents/hard_corps_uprising profile and any portable user_data/ profile separately. When upstream migrates legacy data, it moves the legacy folder by rename, or uses a staged verified copy and then removes the legacy folder after activation; successful migration does not leave the old profile in place. A failed migration falls back to the legacy root for that run and retries on the next startup. If only legacy cleanup fails after activation, portable user_data/ stays active and the legacy folder may remain. An unwritable portable root can also fall back to the system root. --user_data_root=<folder> selects that root without migration; --cache_root can select a separate cache. Preserve every active root and the separate backups. Portcove does not manage their backup, rollback, compatibility or deletion.

listings.name: Icewind Dale II (GemRB)
listings.summary: Set up Icewind Dale II through its upstream gemrb player using your own original files. Setup, profiles and updates stay upstream-owned.

steps.title: Use this original game and edition
steps.instruction: Use a complete installed original Icewind Dale II working copy. Icewind Dale I, Enhanced Edition and the included trivial demo are different inputs. Keep your originals elsewhere unchanged; upstream handles its own data recognition and preparation. A Portcove registration does not authenticate original-game files.

steps.title: Prepare upstream and select the real player
steps.instruction: Use a complete upstream GemRB build with its plugins, scripts and supplied configuration, not just a loose executable. GitHub release metadata has no binary asset to recommend. Give this game its own configuration: GamePath points to a separate complete working copy of the installed original; GameType=iwd2. Use the configuration supplied with your actual build rather than leaving @...@ development-template placeholders. Register gemrb.exe with the complete GemRB installation as working directory and two literal argument lines, -c then the absolute path to this game’s configuration.

steps.title: Keep the actual original and player data
steps.instruction: Choose a dedicated empty private CachePath for this game: GemRB clears that directory, so it must never be your originals, saves or profile root. SavePath is the parent containing save/, not save/ itself. Keep a separate SavePath per game. GemRB can also write gem-*.ini into GamePath before trying SavePath, so preserve and use a working data copy; SavePath alone does not isolate original installation writes. Preserve that working copy, actual save/config locations and mods with GemRB closed before updates. Do not move saves between different games or editions.

steps.title: Add the game and manage your files
steps.instruction: Finish setup with the project’s tools before adding the game. Portcove saves your selected executable, working folder and launch arguments; choose Play separately when you are ready. You manage this game’s files, original files and profile. Removing its registration leaves those files in place. Portcove does not offer updates, backups, rollback, data migration or file deletion for this external copy. Keep a working copy and its data before changing versions. Other platforms need their own supported application and setup instructions.

warnings: GemRB clears its cache directory. Use a dedicated private CachePath, separate from original files, saves and profile roots.

listings.name: Mario Party 6 (Starlit Party)
listings.summary: Attach an independently permitted, prepared Starlit Party Windows player for your own Mario Party 6 USA disc. Preserve its actual working-directory saves and content root; limited minigame coverage and title-specific launcher/font permission scope remain explicit.

steps.title: Prepare your own USA disc upstream
steps.instruction: Use a complete copy and components you are independently permitted to use. Finish upstream preparation outside Portcove, keep independent originals and recovery copies. No original, helper, compiler or game is obtained or executed by this guide. Use your own Mario Party 6 USA GameCube disc image or matching extracted disc tree. Complete the supported upstream content import and configuration first, retaining the independent original and any selected external content root. Another region or Mario Party game is not admitted by the shared engine. The Windows native player, Android APK and browser/iPhone experience are different artifacts, not a shared native-platform qualification.

steps.title: Keep the complete Windows package
steps.instruction: The inspected official 0.5.0 Windows ZIP contains AMD64 mp6native.exe, renderer libraries, res/ and notices. Keep the complete extracted package. The selected native entry launches the UI and calls GameMain within the same process; do not select a GameCube executable, disc image, browser bundle, Android package or build script. Package presence and source review do not establish complete imports, dependencies or Windows gameplay.

steps.title: Attach the prepared player
steps.instruction: Select mp6native.exe, use its complete extracted package folder as working directory and leave arguments empty. Review and consent to the selected launch details, then choose Play separately, then use the upstream player UI with its already prepared content. Working directory matters: Windows saves are deliberately relative to it. Complete any missing import/preparation outside the attached attempt. Quit the actual game normally; forced termination is not a save-flush guarantee.

steps.title: Preserve actual saves and content configuration
steps.instruction: Keep mp6_config.json beside the executable, the saves/ directory relative to the established working directory, memory-card GCIs, states, logs, renderer caches and the selected external content tree. Preserve old working-directory save roots if they differ from the package directory; do not change CWD without reviewing that effect. Upstream states require the same linked build, while GCIs are durable game saves; neither establishes observed restore compatibility. This guide performs no move, migration, backup or deletion.

steps.title: Retain title-specific permission and font evidence
steps.instruction: Keep docs/PARTYBOARD_PROVENANCE.md, all author credits, res/fonts/LICENSES.txt and runtime/component notices. The selected upstream publicly records its maintainer’s 2026-09-12 confirmation of permission to redistribute the adapted Partyboard launcher and N64 Party font with this MP6 release. It explicitly does not claim a public general license for those foreign materials; this guide does not reuse that confirmation for another project or artifact. Other fonts have separate OFL/Apache terms. Original game code/assets still require a copy you are independently permitted to use.

steps.title: Maintain the external copy and limited scope
steps.instruction: Quit the game normally before changing files; forced termination may not finish saving. After an upstream update, relink and review the changed executable. Removing the registration leaves all external files in place; Portcove does not install, update, roll back, back up or delete this copy. Upstream reports only 49 of 81 minigames playable, with unsupported board minigames skipped after a notice. Portcove has not confirmed minigames, boards, microphone support, saving or gameplay on Windows or other platforms.

warnings: Preserve working-directory saves and exact USA content. Partial minigame coverage and this release’s limited launcher/font permission record do not grant broader support or reuse rights.

listings.name: inFamous (2009 PS3) (inFAMOUSreborn)
listings.summary: An early inFamous PS3 recompilation with setup 1.1. The Windows 10/11 x86-64 Direct3D 12 setup EXE checks or installs build tools, imports your own European BCES00220 ISO or game folder, then generates and compiles locally. Encrypted ISOs need their matching .dkey. A launch announcement does not establish playable progress; Portcove has not confirmed setup or gameplay.

steps.title: Finish the supported European game setup
steps.instruction: Use your own inFamous European PS3 BCES00220 files and complete the upstream Windows setup, translation and build before adding the player. An already decrypted supported folder avoids a key-input route; encrypted images have their separate owner-supplied requirements. This guide provides no keys, decryption or game data. The selected 1.1 Windows setup is a preparation program, not an already compiled game. Windows 10/11 x64, Direct3D 12 and the upstream build/runtime prerequisites remain required.

steps.title: Keep the complete prepared installation
steps.instruction: Retain the full completed port directory, its native inFamous.exe launcher, installer/launch.txt, build-install/inFamousRecomp.exe, the prepared game/ELF, libraries, settings and notices. The producer writes executable, working-directory, argument and environment values into launch.txt. The normal launcher reads those values; selecting the bare game without its published context is not an equivalent shortcut. Keep project/runtime/compiler/component terms separate from original game rights and do not share private translated outputs.

steps.title: Add the native upstream launcher
steps.instruction: Select the completed inFamous.exe in its existing port directory, use that directory as working directory and leave arguments empty. Review the selected program, folder and arguments, then choose Play when ready. Its native launcher supplies the producer-written launch configuration and environment. Portcove observes that launcher only; it can report the launch finished after handoff while inFamousRecomp.exe and helpers still run. Use the game’s own controls to quit and do not interpret the launcher’s exit as full-game completion.

steps.title: Preserve the current saves and launch configuration
steps.instruction: Keep the whole existing port, installer/launch.txt, settings.ini, all original/generated content and gamedata/. Default saves are under gamedata/dev_hdd0/home/00000001/savedata relative to the configured port working directory; retain all profiles, trophies and related data as present. Existing SAVEDATA_ROOT and other producer/user path overrides must remain intact. Do not transplant launch.txt into a different layout, reset populated settings or merge saves merely to add the launcher. No save conversion, migration, backup or restore is performed.

steps.title: Leave updates and recovery upstream
steps.instruction: Close the actual game and helpers before upstream replacement, rebuild, repair or recovery, even if Portcove’s activity has finished. Upstream owns imports, build tools, runtime replacement and launch configuration; review/select the current launcher again after changes. Early-release PPU/SPU, rendering and campaign claims do not establish gameplay/controller/real-save acceptance here. Removing the library reference preserves all external files. No managed installation/update/backup/rollback, full-session tracking or Supported qualification is supplied.

warnings: Select the completed inFamous.exe launcher and preserve installer/launch.txt plus its full port/data directory. Its handoff can outlive Portcove’s activity; close the actual game/helpers before upstream changes. The setup EXE and a context-free bare runtime are separate routes.

listings.name: Infinite Undiscovery Recomp (doc-haz)
listings.summary: Explore Infinite Undiscovery Recomp (doc-haz) and follow the upstream project for requirements, downloads and setup.

steps.title: Import your own game on first Play
steps.instruction: The official Windows x64 ZIP is portable and has no installer. Choose InfiniteUndiscoveryRecomp.exe and keep its DLLs and notices together. On first Play, the game’s integrated wizard validates and imports your own Disc 1 from a supported XDVDFS ISO or extracted folder; Disc 2 and A/B Voucher DLC are optional. It identifies supported USA, USA-UNDUB, Europe, Japan and Asia editions from the media. Do not mix editions. Portcove does not run an extraction helper or developer compiler. Windows 10/11 x64 and Direct3D 12 are required; use Microsoft’s Visual C++ 2015–2022 x64 Redistributable if the documented runtime DLLs are missing.

steps.title: Keep each content profile together
steps.instruction: The complete portable folder holds setup.json and separate USA, USA-UNDUB, EUROPE, JAPAN and ASIA profiles. Each configured profile owns its imported assets/DLC, saves and configuration. Keep cache/runtime.toml too: it contains runtime settings despite the cache folder name. Close the game before updates or copying data. Keep interrupted import/staging folders recoverable and consult upstream; do not merge different editions. Backups can include large original-game files and DLC, so keep them private. The separate IU Save Bridge companion is optional and is not run by Portcove.

steps.title: Update an existing copy safely
steps.instruction: For a copy you register yourself, you or upstream provide updates. Extract a new official player into a separate folder, keep the working copy, and follow the selected release’s instructions for carrying its complete compatible content profiles and setup.json. Do not copy old runtime DLLs or shader caches over the replacement. Runtime rollback does not rewind saves or guarantee that older software can read them. The selected release-tag documentation had not tested the Disc 1 to Disc 2 transition. Later upstream documentation at 614a0a0ebd72103fce8aaa52c715d847b703a53e reports repeated successful transitions, while complete Disc 2 progression and a full playthrough remain unverified and a Vesplume Tower / Orb of Patience softlock remains under investigation. These are upstream reports; Portcove has not run the game.

steps.instruction: Supply your own legally obtained matching gds-0033.chd and 317-0384-com.pic in the included game files directory. steps.title: Add the ordinary native launcher
steps.instruction: Select Initial D Arcade Stage 3 Recompiled.exe, set its complete containing product folder as working directory and leave arguments empty. Review the selected program, folder and arguments, then choose Play when ready and use the upstream launcher. It owns preparation/update prompts and supplies the runtime’s game, card, music, settings and presentation context. Keep its supplied PowerShell/tools and runtime with it; do not select powershell.exe, a PS1 script, the integrity/setup helper or a context-free Runtime.exe as the game. Preserve the upstream 60 FPS starting/default choice and any existing F1 choices rather than forcing experimental presentation.

steps.title: Preserve the whole portable player-data layout
steps.instruction: Keep game files, card data, custom music and logs, idas3_user_settings.ini, update preferences and all other existing user files in the product folder. Preserve card data/InitialD_player_card.card or the existing selected CardImage path and every other card. A card image and a game-state snapshot are separate; do not reset a populated card, merge files, discard pending recovery data or assume that another arcade/Dreamcast build can use it. Portcove performs no card import/conversion, backup, restore or source extraction.

steps.title: Keep maintenance and completion evidence upstream
steps.instruction: The selected native launcher can hand off through helpers. Portcove follows that program only; a finished activity does not prove the runtime/helpers have stopped or make files safe to replace. Quit them before upstream updater, repair or recovery, preserve the previous complete application/data, and review/select the launcher again after changes. Upstream’s update preservation, rollback, card and physical-controller reports are not Portcove observations. Removing the reference preserves external files. Managed installation/update/backup/rollback, full-session tracking and Supported qualification are unavailable; this title’s unfinished acceptance remains explicit.

warnings: Select Initial D Arcade Stage 3 Recompiled.exe with the complete v2489 product folder and your own matching CHD/PIC preparation. Preserve game files, every card, custom music, settings and logs; the runtime and setup scripts require their upstream context.

steps.title: Keep the working engine and your original ISO together
steps.instruction: For the v0.9.81 Windows Static Recomp route, finish the supported upstream setup with your own Melee NTSC-U 1.02 ISO and keep the complete package and required Sys/runtime companions. Source Port is a different engine; do not substitute executables, generated output, mod data or profiles merely because both are in the release. Portcove registration does not authenticate the whole original disc or build private output. Keep the complete original and creating configuration recoverable.

steps.title: Select the direct native player
steps.instruction: Select the working melee_port.exe. Its installation is the normal working directory, but keep a different established working directory when your actual working launch uses one: relative settings, Sys, cards and replays can otherwise point to a new profile. Supply --iso and the absolute path to your original ISO as separate arguments. Retain the actual creating --sys-dir, --settings-path, --card-dir, --replay-dir, --user-dir and any supported renderer/mod arguments rather than inventing a new profile. Do not select a .bat file or MeleeUnlockedLauncher.exe for this direct-player route. Save launch details, then choose Play separately.

steps.title: Finish upstream restarts and replacement separately
steps.instruction: In the inspected v0.9.81 source, release checks and package installation are called by the separate optional launcher, not the direct Static Recomp player. Select that exact direct-player route; this does not qualify older players or the other engine. The game still offers an explicit DLSS model download that can write a DLL for the next restart, and backend/settings changes can start a successor. Complete those optional upstream changes separately before relinking the working player and choosing Play again. Portcove supervises the selected native process and does not adopt successors, install optional model files or own runtime replacement. This route does not disable every network feature or external write. Online Slippi accounts, controller/adapter setup, mods, crash-report sharing and optional DLSS model downloads are separate choices, not automatic Portcove setup.

steps.title: Preserve all engine and shared player data
steps.instruction: Before changing versions keep the whole working installation, Versions, Sys, port-settings.ini, launcher.ini, User/GC/CardA and other actual card folders, replays, practice/lab data, PhobGCC settings, Slippi user/account state, shader/pipeline caches, logs, mods, unknown files and all explicit custom paths. Preserve the actual LOCALAPPDATA/MeleeUnlocked launcher history too. Different engine/version folders can share ISO, settings, cards and replays; they do not establish compatibility or isolation. Upstream owns updates. Portcove registration provides no managed update, backup, rollback, migration or deletion; removing registration leaves all external files untouched.

warnings: Original game data and NVIDIA/Intel/Slippi and other components retain their separate terms. This handoff does not qualify online matches, mod/save compatibility, generated output, gameplay or the optional other engine.

listings.name: Metroid Prime Remastered — Switch edition (MetroidPrimeRemasteredRecomp)

Vertical controller aim is broken, rare loading crashes remain, and physical controllers, HDR and real fullscreen are untested. The Windows x64 ZIP needs Windows 10 v1903+/11 and Vulkan 1.3; only RTX 3080 is tested, with AMD/Intel untested. The official launcher imports your own version 1.0.0 base NSP/XCI/NSZ/XCZ with prod.keys and title.keys where required; updates are not accepted. Those container formats were tested only with synthetic inputs. build_mpr.cmd separately translates source game code; player instructions do not establish whether translated code is already in the release. Exact title/region/hashes are unspecified, with no other desktop route established. Portcove offers no setup or launch integration and has not tested gameplay.

listings.name: Pokémon Legends: Z-A (PokeZ-ARecomp)
listings.summary: An experimental Pokémon Legends: Z-A port derived from LAS, translating AArch64 code to C/x64 with Vulkan. The project reports only Windows/NVIDIA play, with partial Lumiose exploration and battles. Black flashes and night-wall stripes remain; a complete playthrough is unconfirmed. The Windows ZIP launcher is described as a game-free player, generator, importer and compiler that imports and recompiles your own files locally once. Windows 10 v1903+/11 x64 needs Vulkan 1.3; AVX2 is preferred, with a slower SSE4.2 fallback. Inherited Linux/Mac builds are untested for Z-A. Use your own version 1.0.0 base XCI/NSP, optional 2.0.0 update and owned DLC, with prod.keys/title.keys. Firmware fonts are optional; the Windows fallback lacks button icons. Back up before save conversion: 2.0.0 saves cannot load on 1.0.0. Portcove offers no setup or launch integration and has not tested gameplay.

listings.name: Pokémon: Let’s Go, Eevee! (letsgo-recomp)
listings.summary: An in-development Pokémon: Let’s Go port translating AArch64 code to C with an LAS-based Vulkan player. Eevee 1.0.0 has more testing than Pikachu; a full playthrough is unconfirmed. Online, Poké Ball Plus and player 2 are unsupported. Higher frame rates, frame generation and wild battles are experimental. The Windows ZIP launcher imports, copies and recompiles your game locally once; keep one folder per game. Windows 10/11 x64 needs SSE4.2 and Vulkan 1.3, with AVX2 recommended. Other native desktop routes are unconfirmed. Supply your own corresponding Eevee or Pikachu extracted ExeFS/RomFS from any region. Base 1.0.0 enables all options; 1.0.1/1.0.2 have fewer options and less testing. Extract XCI/NSP externally first. No separate keys/firmware input is described after extraction. Portcove offers no setup or launch integration and has not tested gameplay.

Fresh acquisition remains held on the actual title/runtime-fork grant condition: the separate RecompOne-fork and title modifications do not inherit the parent engine’s MIT grant automatically. Before changing versions, close the game and its companion programs and keep the working copy and its data.

This is an early upstream runtime, not a completed-game qualification. Upstream reports incomplete boot/intro control timing, autosave disabled, sound unknown and later missions untested. The canonical runtime-maturity acceptance remains open. This guide supplies neither a gameplay/save observation nor Windows support and does not change the approved scheduling.

references.title: Generation and file ownership
references.instruction: The upstream player loads its generated assembly in the same process. Core imports no original, runs no game compiler and does not own the generated cache. You manage setup, game replacement and recovery using the project’s tools. Portcove does not offer updates, backups, rollback, conversion, data migration or deletion for this external copy. Removing its registration leaves external files in place. Review and select the changed executable before playing again.

references.title: Profile, generated build and save locations
references.instruction: Upstream sets the application data identity to Tenchu. Its documented normal Linux profile is ~/.local/share/Tenchu; an upstream-selected custom save folder can change the effective location. Preserve the entire actual profile and both separately configurable build and save roots. The normal build root is UserData.Dir/game; the selected build root holds Recompiled source, Tenchu.dll and .stamp. settings.json remembers the choices; cards are named from the disc basename with .srm and .srm2 extensions. Retain those files, settings, optional user-supplied font, backups and temporary files, plus the original disc, runtime and every custom root. The display font is not distributed and can fall back to an installed face. Keep the upstream-established writable locations when using an AppImage and preserve any deliberately shared save location; Core does not relocate or rewrite those paths.

listings.download_block_reason: The selected Tenchu title source and published Linux ZIP provide no applicable grant for separately authored title and RecompOne-fork modifications; the project references that separate fork without a public pinned source/grant. The original engine’s MIT licence does not settle this scope. Fresh acquisition stays held until attributable applicable permission/source correspondence or a reviewed permitted replacement resolves it. A separately permitted self-contained copy remains a distinct case; no permission is granted by this guide.

listings.name: Zelda II: The Adventure of Link / z2rs (troyedwardsjr)
listings.summary: Explore Zelda II: The Adventure of Link / z2rs (troyedwardsjr) and follow the upstream project for requirements, downloads and setup.

steps.title: Keep the Windows release archive intact
steps.instruction: Use the complete z2rs-0.6.0-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip folder with z2rs-launcher.exe, z2rs.exe, companions and notices. z2-signal.exe is an optional signalling server, not the player. This is a Rust reconstruction with a native desktop frontend; upstream frame-comparison and enhancement claims do not establish a Portcove playthrough or native/controller observation.

steps.title: Provide your own exact USA ROM
steps.instruction: In the upstream launcher choose your own Zelda II: The Adventure of Link (USA) NES ROM. Its accepted ROM body, after stripping the 16-byte iNES header, has CRC32 BA322865 and SHA-1 11333adb723a5975e0ecca3aee8f4747aa8d2d26. These identify the body, not the complete headered file. The game reads the ROM in place and remembers its path; keep it at that location. The project’s MIT code grant and original-ROM/HD-pack rights are separate; no ROM or extracted asset redistribution is granted.

steps.title: Add the ordinary native launcher
steps.instruction: Select z2rs-launcher.exe, use its complete release directory as working directory and leave arguments empty. Review the selected program, folder and arguments, then choose Play when ready and use the launcher’s ROM picker and Play control. Keep z2rs.exe beside it. After a remembered ROM exists, selecting z2rs.exe with the same directory and empty arguments is an upstream direct-player alternative. Preserve any existing Advanced game-binary override or Z2RS_GAME_BIN choice; do not substitute the server helper.

steps.title: Preserve settings and all save slots
steps.instruction: Keep %APPDATA%/z2rs on Windows, or the existing XDG_DATA_HOME/z2rs override, including z2-native.json, battery saves, savestate*.z2snap and other user files. Preserve the original ROM’s separate path, optional HD packs, randomizer outputs and existing custom config paths. Do not assume save-state compatibility beyond upstream’s documented format, import another project’s saves or reset populated options to add the reference. The ROM is not copied into the default data directory.

steps.title: Leave optional services and maintenance upstream
steps.instruction: Online co-op, the signalling service, HD packs and Discord presence are upstream options; Portcove does not enable services, supply credentials or configure them. The launcher starts a separate game process: Portcove follows the selected program only, and its activity can finish while the game continues. Close the actual game and helpers before replacing the complete upstream release or recovering files. Review/select the executable after updates. Reference removal preserves external files; managed updates, save conversion, backup, rollback, full-session tracking and Supported qualification are unavailable.

warnings: Select z2rs-launcher.exe in the complete Windows release folder and supply your own exact USA ROM. Preserve %APPDATA%/z2rs and the ROM’s original path; the selected launcher does not establish full-game lifetime.

steps.title: Prepare upstream and select the real player
steps.instruction: Use the official upstream download/setup route or a complete already prepared OpenXcom player, keeping its common data and standard mod resources. No GitHub release package was observed. Complete original-data and game selection through upstream before saving the player entry. Register openxcom.exe with its installation folder as working directory, retaining the upstream game selection rather than inventing a fixed argument. steps.title: Keep your originals and game data
steps.instruction: Windows normally uses the actual Documents/OpenXcom user/config location; an installation-local user folder and explicit -data/-user/-config choices can change the searched locations. Preserve every actual selected data/user/config folder, including UFO/TFTD resources, mods, savegames and screenshots. Keep the two original games and their campaigns distinct even if they share one player/profile. Back up with OpenXcom closed before changing runtime or mods.

steps.title: Add the game and manage your files
steps.instruction: Finish setup with the project’s tools before adding the game. Portcove saves your selected executable, working folder and launch arguments; choose Play separately when you are ready. You manage this game’s files, original files and profile. Removing its registration leaves those files in place. Portcove does not offer updates, backups, rollback, data migration or file deletion for this external copy. Keep a working copy and its data before changing versions. Other platforms need their own supported application and setup instructions.

listings.name: Until Dawn (2015 PS4 original) — UntilDawn_PC (SuperCatElvis) (SuperCatElvis)
listings.summary: Information only. The project retains a complete-playthrough claim on its i9-12900KF/RTX 3090 Ti development PC. WIP 0.1.4 adds a renderer thread, faster rendering, a hair fix and more movie skipping, with missing Skip text still noted. The new renderer has only been played on NVIDIA; RX 9070 XT observations concern WIP 0.1.3. Reported scenes range from about 60 FPS in light scenes to 35–45 FPS in busy scenes and 21–25 FPS at the heaviest points. Shader pauses, crashes, temporary deformation, motion drift and graphics defects remain. Renderer_thread=0 is the project’s fallback for threading regressions. Intel graphics are untested; native 4K and stable 60 FPS are goals. New downloads are unavailable while closed-source runtime provenance and distribution rights for game-derived shaders/icon remain unresolved. Original CUSA02636/update 01.03 and a native description do not resolve that condition. Portcove has not confirmed setup or gameplay.
listings.download_block_reason: New downloads are unavailable while the closed-source player’s distribution/provenance remains unresolved, including declared game-derived shader programs and its icon. A native description or own-disc requirement does not approve those files. Information about original CUSA02636/update 01.03 and project-reported progress is retained under this entry’s existing identity. Exact package/source provenance must be resolved before downloads are offered.

steps.title: Use the full experimental Windows tester package
steps.instruction: Keep VS-NativePort-0.0.11-win-x64.zip intact with VS.Launcher.exe, VS.Desktop.exe, VS.Extract.exe, runtime DLLs, resources, licenses and release.json. This is an unfinished Vagrant Story port for Windows 10 1903+/11 x64, with gameplay, cutscene, rendering and audio limits. Native game saves and memory-card/ending conversion are different contracts; complete original memory-card support is not established. No finished-game, native/controller, real-save or Supported acceptance is claimed.

steps.title: Complete the upstream exact-disc and converter checks
steps.instruction: Supply your own USA SLUS-01040 single-track MODE2/2352 disc as BIN, supported CUE/BIN or parentless single-data-track CHD. The decompressed BIN must be exactly 750,643,152 bytes, SHA-256 25221D7F8FDB2C4490AF12D9E82F0E58BDD6ACB43387F9082B3C5E79DFE090C0, SHA-1 38C63DB6C49A06B91D87CD5A4E31B1EC68FE212C. A matching name is insufficient; CHD hashes apply to its decoded content, not container bytes. Complete upstream Start-Game.cmd dependency checks and launcher setup first, including an explicitly chosen compatible FFmpeg with the required encoders. Software installation and original/converter acquisition remain separate user/upstream actions, not Portcove operations.

steps.title: Add the ordinary native launcher
steps.instruction: Select VS.Launcher.exe in the complete tester folder, use that containing folder as working directory and leave arguments empty. Review the selected program, folder and arguments, then choose Play when ready. Use the upstream disc, save-folder and converter pickers and its Play control. The launcher verifies the full image for each Play, prepares assets and starts VS.Desktop.exe with their context. Do not substitute VS.Extract.exe, Start-Game.cmd, a converter, or context-free VS.Desktop.exe as the same route; no integrity refusal is bypassed.

steps.title: Keep per-user prepared assets and separately selected saves
steps.instruction: Preserve the full %APPDATA%/VS-NativePort/VagrantStory directory with prepared assets, completion inventories, launcher selections, logs and retained failed/replaced staging as present. Also retain the exact game-save folder you selected, including slot00.vssave through slot99.vssave and recoverable .bak files as present; it is independent of installed program files and prepared assets. Keep the original disc available for later verification and preserve custom --save-dir choices. Do not delete retained failure directories, merge original memory cards or reset path selections to register the game. Portcove performs no source conversion, save migration, backup or restore.

steps.title: Leave updater and recovery ownership upstream
steps.instruction: The launcher owns its offered update checks, consent and replacement/recovery flow; registration does not select an update or install FFmpeg. Quit the actual game/helpers before maintenance or recovery, retain prior complete program/data/save copies and review/select the current launcher after changes. Portcove observes the selected launcher only; a finished activity does not prove all child processes stopped. Removing its reference preserves external files. Managed installation/update/backup/rollback, full-session tracking and Supported qualification are not offered. CC0 project terms, retained earlier GPL grants, third-party libraries and original-game rights remain separate.

warnings: Select VS.Launcher.exe in the complete Windows tester package after upstream dependency/disc setup. Keep the exact USA image, %APPDATA%/VS-NativePort/VagrantStory assets and independently selected save folder; experimental limits and original memory-card conversion remain explicit.

steps.title: Prepare the supported USA two-disc original
steps.instruction: Use your own Valkyrie Profile USA discs, Disc 1 SLUS-01156 and Disc 2 SLUS-01179, as complete CUE/BIN sets. The source lists both discs in a roster and boots the first program.
